sections.content:
43,965 people

were counted on the census as "legal associate professionals" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Legal associate professionals provide administrative support for legal professionals and investigate and make recommendations on legal matters that do not fall within the province of a normal court of law.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "legal associate professionals" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "legal associate professionals", 14.7% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "legal associate professionals" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.footer: Source: Census 2021 from Office for National Statistics

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "legal associate professionals" included:

  • transport and distribution clerks and assistants
  • stock control clerks and assistants
  • sales administrators

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "legal associate professionals" there were more women than men (66.7% compared with 33.3%).

This means "legal associate professionals" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "business and public service associate professionals".

Men made up 33.3% and women made up 66.7% of "legal associate professionals"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "legal associate professionals" included:

  • teaching professionals (other)
  • health services and public health managers and directors
  • tailors and dressmakers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "legal associate professionals" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "legal associate professionals" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "legal associate professionals", 10.4% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (80.4% compared with 19.6%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (93.2%) than self-employed (6.8%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Leeds, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
